clue.text: Neat electrical network keeps farm animals in a field

definitions.text: keeps farm animals in a field

parts.note: neat is an old word for oxen or bovine livestock
the national grid is the electricity distribution network

explanation.surface: Tidy wiring hidden on a farm somehow keeps the animals in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' looks like an adjective meaning tidy, but it is the archaic noun for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: A grid of bars over a pit across a road stops livestock crossing out of their pasture.

indicators.note: other signals that each is turned into a different arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: Two lovers pine for one another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'other' looks like part of the phrase 'each other', but it rearranges EACH.
explanation.definitionFit: To ache for something is to long for it.

parts.note: plain looks like the adverb meaning simply, but it is the noun for flat land

explanation.definitionFit: The treeless Arctic lowland with permanently frozen subsoil is a cold flat expanse.

clue.text: Upsets Alice, for example, when describing some poetry

indicators.note: upsets signals that the letters are knocked over into a new order

parts.note: eg is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: A girl called Alice gets upset by a sad poem.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective applies to mournful verse, a lament for the dead.

explanation.surface: Advance and assault the enemy.
explanation.definitionFit: To fence off land with posts and bars is to enclose it, and to rail at someone is to berate them.

clue.text: Hooted at performance after free admission

indicators.note: admission signals one word being let into another

parts.note: a deed is an act or performance
to rid is to free

explanation.surface: An audience jeered at a show after getting in without paying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performance after free admission' reads as getting into a show for nothing; 'admission' is really the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To deride is to mock or jeer, as an audience hooting does.

explanation.surface: A copy that is exactly alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheet made using inked paper is a copy, and figuratively a thing identical to another.

parts.note: chic means stylish or smart
Hester is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A fashionable young woman living in town.
explanation.definitionFit: Chichester is a cathedral city in West Sussex, in southern England.

explanation.surface: A home match scheduled for a city football team.
explanation.definitionFit: A tub is plumbed into a house, and the Somerset spa town is a city.

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of hire candle are put out of order

explanation.surface: Rent a candle to go out for lighting.
explanation.definitionFit: A hanging branched fitting holding many bulbs or candles is a decorative lamp.

clue.text: It describes a foot in metres

definitions.text: It describes a foot in metres

parts.words: It describes a foot in metres
parts.note: foot and metres look like units of length, but in poetry a foot is a group of syllables and metres are rhythmic patterns

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective names verse built from the short-long unit, the commonest metrical foot in English.

clue.text: Not birds, they chirp and fly

definitions.text: Not birds, they chirp and fly

parts.words: Not birds, they chirp and fly
parts.note: something that flies and chirps sounds avian, but these are insects that make a shrill noise

explanation.definitionFit: These are large insects whose males produce a loud buzzing song in warm weather.

parts.note: cheap means inexpensive
skate is a flat fish

explanation.surface: A bargain-basement fish is just right for a miser.
explanation.definitionFit: A stingy person who avoids spending would happily buy the cheapest fish.

parts.note: points to Lancelot Brown, the 18th-century English landscape gardener known by this nickname, which also means skill

explanation.definitionFit: The word means ability, and was the famous nickname of the landscape designer Brown.

clue.text: But they're no disgrace to musicians

definitions.text: But they're no disgrace to musicians

parts.words: But they're no disgrace to musicians
parts.note: insults bring disgrace, but in music these are curved marks joining notes to be played smoothly

explanation.definitionFit: The word means slanders, and in notation also means curved lines telling players to join notes.

clue.text: Income from flat in French street

indicators.note: in places the word for flat inside the word for street

parts.note: rue is French for street
even means flat or level

explanation.surface: Earnings from renting out an apartment in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: Revenue is money coming in, especially to a government or company.

clue.text: Dance and a drink to uplift a sailor

parts.note: rum is an alcoholic drink

indicators.note: in a down clue, uplifting the word for sailor means reading it upwards, so backwards

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A dance, and a tot of rum to cheer up a seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance.

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword stand-in for many
to laud is to praise

explanation.surface: Someone widely admired.
explanation.definitionFit: Claud is a man's name, a spelling of Claude.

parts.note: E is a musical key
a spy is a secret agent

explanation.surface: Go and meet an important operative.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of something.

explanation.surface: A ship has departed from the dock.
explanation.definitionFit: Port is the left side of a ship, and also a harbour town or haven.

parts.note: a gift for something suggests talent, but here it is a present given to buy corrupt favour

explanation.definitionFit: A bribe is money or a favour offered to make someone act improperly.

parts.note: a mother bore her child, so the phrase reading bore a youngster describes this animal

explanation.definitionFit: A baby animal of the ursine kind, whose mother carried and gave birth to it.

clue.text: Sees trouble, grabs a hat, and gets out

indicators.note: grabs means one word clutches the other inside it
trouble signals that the letters of sees are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: a cap is a hat

explanation.surface: Someone senses danger, seizes a hat and flees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges the first word to ESES, and 'grabs' wraps that round the hat.
explanation.definitionFit: To escape is to break free or get away.

parts.note: dashed reads as a mild curse, but it points to the wall rendering called pebbledash

explanation.definitionFit: Small smooth stones, the kind thrown onto wet render in pebbledash, a British wall finish.

clue.text: Years possibly follow as a metal tester

indicators.note: follow places the rearranged years after the word as
possibly suggests the letters of years could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Years might pass with someone working as a metal tester.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges the given word, and 'follow' sets the result after the two-letter word.
explanation.definitionFit: An assay is a test of the purity of gold or silver, and this person performs it.

indicators.note: hold means the words rank Arabs contain the answer within them

explanation.surface: A capital city where Arabs of rank are in control.
explanation.definitionFit: Ankara is the capital city of Turkey.

clue.text: He finishes off the game with the queen

definitions.text: He finishes off the game with the queen

parts.words: He finishes off the game with the queen
parts.note: reads like a chess move checkmating with the queen, but describes someone who finishes others off

explanation.definitionFit: A murderer finishes people off; the word also names a darts or pool game and a Queen song.

clue.text: Sailing vessel with a professional second mate

indicators.note: second places the letter a in the next position after the professional

parts.note: pro is short for professional

explanation.surface: A boat crewed by a skilled second mate.
explanation.definitionFit: A proa is a Malay outrigger sailing boat.

clue.text: Above the neck-in a glass of beer?

explanation.surface: Is the froth above the neck of the bottle?
explanation.definitionFit: The skull sits on top of the neck, and the foam on poured beer is its froth.

clue.text: He holds hands during the game

definitions.text: He holds hands during the game

parts.words: He holds hands during the game
parts.note: holding hands sounds romantic, but hands here are the sets of cards dealt to each player

explanation.definitionFit: Someone playing bridge or poker holds a hand of cards throughout.

explanation.surface: A betting scheme for moving things around.
explanation.definitionFit: The tote is the pool-betting system at racecourses for a person who bets, and to tote is to carry.

clue.text: Metal shackles keep men in step

definitions.text: Metal shackles keep men in step

parts.words: Metal shackles keep men in step
parts.note: shackles of metal suggest prisoners chained together, but these are groups playing brass instruments for marchers

explanation.definitionFit: Ensembles of trumpets, cornets and tubas set the beat for marching soldiers.
